title: The DPO loss
goal:
Implement the DPO loss (Section 4, Equation 7) for a batch of preference pairs:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{DPO}} = -\log \sigma\!\Big(\beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta(y_w \mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y_w \mid x)} - \beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta(y_l \mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y_l \mid x)}\Big)$$

The inputs are the sequence log-probabilities `pi_w`, `pi_l`, `ref_w`, and `ref_l`, each an array of shape `(B,)` (one entry per pair), and a float `beta`. Write two functions:

- `reward_margin(pi_w, pi_l, ref_w, ref_l, beta)` returns the array $\hat r_\theta(x, y_w) - \hat r_\theta(x, y_l)$, where $\hat r_\theta = \beta \log(\pi_\theta / \pi_{\text{ref}})$.
- `dpo_loss(pi_w, pi_l, ref_w, ref_l, beta)` returns the per-pair losses, shape `(B,)`, not their mean. The function must stay finite when the margin is $\pm 1000$.
hints: The margin is `beta * ((pi_w - ref_w) - (pi_l - ref_l))`. The reference terms enter with the opposite sign of the policy terms.
$-\log\sigma(m) = \log(1 + e^{-m})$. Written as `np.log(1 + np.exp(-m))`, it overflows for $m = -1000$.
